summary: Extends vCard so an address-book entry can hold an instant messaging or presence address as a URI. As IM grows, people want to save those contacts alongside phone numbers and email. It was replaced by RFC 6350.

eli5.summary: An address book has spots for phone and email. This adds a spot for chat names too. It was later replaced by a newer version of vCard.

questions: how to store im address in vcard
how do i add a chat address to a contact card
subtitle: Add instant messaging addresses to digital contact cards.

tldr.problem: As instant messaging became common, people wanted to store IM contact addresses in their digital address books alongside phone numbers and email, but vCard had no field for it.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4770 adds an IMPP (Instant Messaging and Presence Protocol) type to vCard that holds a URI pointing to an IM or presence service, with optional parameters to indicate whether it is for personal or business use.
tldr.outcome: vCard address books can now include IM contact information. RFC 6350 later superseded this with a revised vCard format.

facts.label: Supported parameters
facts.value: TYPE (PERSONAL, BUSINESS, HOME, WORK, MOBILE, PREF)

today: RFC 4770 was obsoleted by RFC 6350, which provided a revised vCard format. However, the IMPP extension remains a widely recognized way to include instant messaging contact information in address books.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The vCard is a standard format for storing contact information, defined in RFC 2425 and RFC 2426. It holds names, phone numbers, email addresses and other details about a person in a portable format. As instant messaging (IM) and presence protocol (PP) applications became widespread, users wanted to save IM contact information in their address books alongside this other data.

RFC 4770 extends vCard with a new field type called IMPP (Instant Messaging and Presence Protocol). This allows a URI that identifies an IM or presence address to be stored in a vCard, just like email and phone numbers. A single vCard can contain multiple IMPP entries, and each entry can specify what kind of communication it is best for.
sections.eli5: vCard is how your computer stores contact information. This adds a new type of contact information: instant messaging addresses, like a chat app username or ID.

sections.title: The IMPP Type and Its Parameters
sections.content:
The IMPP type entry in a vCard contains a single URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) that points to an IM or PP service. The scheme of the URI indicates which protocol to use. Common examples include sip: for SIP/SIMPLE, xmpp: for XMPP, irc: for IRC, ymsgr: for Yahoo Messenger, msn: for Microsoft Messenger, aim: for AOL Instant Messenger, or im: and pres: for CPIM and CPP gateways.

IMPP entries can include optional TYPE parameters that describe when the address should be used. These include PERSONAL or BUSINESS to indicate the communication context, and HOME, WORK, or MOBILE to indicate the device or location. The PREF parameter marks a preferred address, similar to how it works for telephone numbers.
sections.eli5: An IMPP entry is like an email or phone field: it has an address and optional labels saying if it is for work, home, mobile, or if it is your preferred contact method.

sections.title: Example Usage
sections.content:
A simple vCard with an IMPP entry might look like this: it declares a vCard for Alice Doe and includes an IMPP entry with the URI im:alice@example.com, marked as personal and preferred. The recipient would know to use an instant messaging protocol to reach Alice at that address.

Different IM systems can be stored in separate IMPP entries within the same vCard. For example, one entry might use xmpp: for XMPP-based messaging, another sip: for SIP/SIMPLE calling, and another aim: for AOL Instant Messenger. This flexibility lets users share multiple IM contact options without duplicating their vCard structure.
sections.eli5: You can add an IMPP field to a contact card saying 'you can reach me at alice@example.com on instant messaging', just like you would add an email address.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content:
RFC 4770 formally registers the IMPP type with IANA as an extension to the text/directory MIME type. The registration specifies that IMPP contains a single URI, that the type parameter can include purpose and location hints, and that the intended usage is COMMON, meaning it is expected to be widely used in vCard implementations.

The registration was requested through the IETF MIME Direct mailing list in October 2004 and documents the type name, purpose, encoding, allowed parameters and special notes for implementers.
sections.eli5: The Internet organization IANA officially added IMPP to the list of valid vCard field types so that all contact card systems would recognize and support it.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
RFC 4770 does not introduce new security issues beyond those present in the vCard specification itself. However, the RFC notes an important consideration: many people regard their presence and instant messaging information as more sensitive than their phone numbers or email addresses. Revealing when someone is online or available can expose personal information about their habits and schedule.

Any system that stores, exchanges, or transfers vCards needs to carefully manage the privacy of IM contact information and protect it with the same care given to other personal data.
sections.eli5: Knowing if someone is online right now tells you a lot about when they are free. So IM contact information needs to be kept private and secure, just like passwords.
